title: The pin
line: A piece cannot move without exposing a bigger one behind it.

steps.text: The bishop on g5 pins the knight on f6. If the knight moves, the queen behind it on d8 can be taken.
When the piece behind is the king, the pinned piece may not move at all: that would leave the king in check.
Pin the black queen to her king: move your rook onto the line they stand on.
steps.hint: The queen and the king stand on the same line.
steps.after: The queen cannot step off that line. She can take the rook, and then the king takes her.

steps.text: Tap the black piece that cannot move because of a pin.
steps.after: The knight shields its king from the bishop.

steps.text: A pinned piece cannot run, so attack it with a pawn.
steps.hint: Your center pawn can attack the knight in one move.
steps.after: The knight cannot move, and the pawn takes it next.

steps.text: Only pieces that move along lines can pin: the bishop, the rook and the queen.

summary: A pinned piece cannot move without exposing what stands behind it. Attack it, and it cannot run.
